sections.summary: The neutral reading finds this section marks the transition from theological exposition to ethical exhortation, urging the recipients to walk worthy of their calling with humility, gentleness, patience, and mutual forbearance in love, maintaining the Spirit-created unity in the bond of peace.

The neutral reading finds this section enumerates seven unities that define the community's identity -- one body, one Spirit, one hope, one Lord, one faith, one baptism, one God and Father of all -- forming a creedal summary that provides the theological ground for the exhortation to unity.

The neutral reading finds this section describes Christ's distribution of specific gifts to each member of the community, supported by a modified citation of Psalm 68:18 applied to Christ's ascent and gift-giving, with the gifted persons identified as apostles, prophets, evangelists, and shepherd-teachers.

sections.section_title: The Purpose of the Gifts -- Building Up the Body
sections.summary: The neutral reading finds this section describes the purpose of Christ's gifted persons: to equip the saints for ministry and build up the body toward corporate maturity -- the measure of the stature of the fullness of Christ -- so that the community grows from instability toward truth-speaking in love, with each part contributing to the whole under Christ's headship.

sections.section_title: The Gentile Way of Life to Be Abandoned
sections.summary: The neutral reading finds this section diagnoses the unconverted Gentile condition as a causal chain: hardened heart produces ignorance, which produces alienation from God's life, which produces darkened understanding, which produces a futile way of life ending in callousness, sensuality, and insatiable impurity.

sections.section_title: The Contrast -- What the Recipients Learned
sections.summary: The neutral reading finds this section describes the three-part transformation the recipients were taught: putting off the old humanity with its deceitful desires, being renewed in the spirit of the mind, and putting on the new humanity created according to God in true righteousness and holiness -- with the 'new humanity' echoing the 'one new humanity' created in 2:15.

sections.section_title: The Specific Behaviors of the New Humanity
sections.summary: The neutral reading finds this section provides specific ethical instructions flowing from the put-off/put-on transformation -- truth-telling, anger management, honest labor, edifying speech, and mutual forgiveness -- with 4:30 warning against grieving the Holy Spirit 'by whom you were sealed for the day of redemption,' drawing on the background of Isaiah 63:10 where Israel's grieving of God's Spirit caused God to turn against them.
sections.relevance: Verse 4:30 is conventionally cited as proof of permanent security: the Spirit sealed believers 'for the day of redemption,' guaranteeing they will reach that day regardless of conduct. The neutral reading reveals the verse functions as an ethical warning embedded in practical instruction. The seal is invoked not to guarantee permanence but to heighten the gravity of the command: do not grieve the very Spirit who sealed you. The Isaiah 63:10 background is significant -- Israel 'rebelled and grieved his Holy Spirit; therefore he turned to be their enemy and himself fought against them.' The neutral reading notes the logic is 'consequential, not transactional,' calling for conduct that honors the sealing. Yet the prophetic background implies the relationship signified by the seal is not unaffected by persistent grieving. The conventional reading isolates 'sealed for the day of redemption' as a guarantee while ignoring both the warning context and the Isaiah background suggesting serious consequences for the very conduct being warned against.
